correctness.rationale: For the stated weighted Laplacian, the uniform-cycle inverse sends e_0-e_4 to an antisymmetric vector with amplitudes (x+2)/Q and 1/Q on A and B, and zero on C. The rank-one Downdate denominator is D/Q>0; this gives the three stated diagonals and strict A>B>C diagonal ordering. The trace gain is the negative log derivative of the diagonal. Independently setting N=(x^2+3x+1)D and d=1-w gives G_B/G_C=1+dx/N and G_A/G_C=1+(x+2)^2 dx/N. Expanding the derivatives recovers the stated polynomials as F=xN'-N and J=((x+2)^2-1)F-2(x+2)x(N+dx). F increases from a negative constant and J has one coefficient sign change and opposite endpoint signs. At the B=C score crossing, (dx/N)'=0 but the A-to-C diagonal ratio is increasing, so R_A<R_B=R_C; hence that crossing comes strictly before the A=B crossing. This proves the whole minimizer and tie classification. I verified both rational root brackets at w=1/2. Three- and four-cycles with one exceptional edge have at most two reflection orbits; no broader minimality is implied. RESULT.md, proof steps 1–5, is a replay path; the supplied script was inspected, not executed.

evidence: The general Nyström treatment supplies the objective and selection framework, not a classification on weak-edge cycles. The cone result proves a hub-to-periphery switch for a cone; the half-line result gives a rank-one capture staircase and finite-path shifts.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The five-cycle has no universal vertex and is not a cone, a path, or a half-line. Those screening results are not stronger theorems on a class containing this graph.

evidence: The star theorem already exhibits trace optimization migrating with screening while the selected determinant favors leaves. The prior objective formulas distinguish a log slope from a level after the resolvent identity is applied.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither generic nonequivalence nor the existence of a screening switch is asserted as new. The all-weight strict ordering of two separate crossings on a graph with three candidate orbits requires additional comparisons not implied by the inspected statements.

evidence: Belabbas–Wolfe Proposition 4.2 identifies the trace residual with the trace of a Schur complement. Krause–Singh–Guestrin distinguish determinant and trace design objectives on PDF pp. 2 and 22. The inspected catalogue cycle theorem treats unweighted uniformly screened cycles.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The equivalent pinned-precision objective is the trace of the inverse of the screened principal minor after deleting the chosen vertex. The entropy criterion for the singleton is instead just its marginal variance. Standard objective equivalences do not classify the weighted cycle; the vertex-transitive case has no distinct singleton orbits.

evidence: The exact defective-five-cycle hit is the frozen record itself. The distinct cycle and star findings state optimizer laws for different weight or graph regimes; they do not tabulate the two crossing roots for this family.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The comparison sought the symbolic two-boundary, all-w classification, not a single numerical threshold. The same-day distinct entries were assessed by their statements, not their dates.

originality.rationale: Trace/determinant disagreement and screening-driven migration are already known in other graph families. The supported distinctive claim is the exact three-orbit, two-boundary singleton classification for every weak-edge weight on the five-cycle, together with its fixed determinant optimum. No stronger covering statement was established in the inspected sources.
residual_risks: An equivalent result stated as one-pin trace minimization of a screened weighted Laplacian could exist outside the inspected design literature.
The comparison establishes distinct content in the inspected sources, not publication priority among catalogue entries.

The exact and universal two-threshold law is useful beyond exhibiting generic design-objective disagreement: it identifies every screening interval and both tie sets where a one-landmark choice changes even though marginal-variance ordering does not.
